One way governments can charge firms for pollution rights is by imposing a per-unit tax on emissions. A tax (or price in this case) of $[tax amount] per ton of radioactive waste emitted will achieve the desired level of pollution. A. $90 B. $120 C. $150 D. $180
questions_and_answers.answer: Final Answer: it represents the tax amount that would achieve the desired level of pollution control, specifically the socially optimal quantity of radioactive waste , which is 360 million tons per day. Therefore, the correct answer is option B) $120. ; Explanation: To calculate this, we can use the concept of Pigouvian taxation , which is designed to internalize the external costs associated with pollution. In this case, the government wants to reduce radioactive waste emissions to the socially optimal level. By setting a tax per ton of waste, firms will be incentivized to reduce their emissions to minimize their tax liability . One way governments can charge firms for pollution rights is by imposing a per-unit tax on emissions. A tax of $27 per ton of sulfur dioxide emitted will achieve the desired level of pollution. Because when the price of emitting a ton of sulfur dioxide is $27 , then power stations will demand a quantity of 350 million tons of sulfur dioxide.
